findings.message: BivariateRenderer imports LAYER_BIVARIATE_PREFIX and SOURCE_BIVARIATE_PREFIX from a module that does not export them, so the type check fails and the bundle will not build. Bivariate and MCDA layers cannot render at all. Line 2: `import { LAYER_BIVARIATE_PREFIX, SOURCE_BIVARIATE_PREFIX } from './constants';`. BivariateRenderer/constants.ts exports only SOURCE_LAYER_BIVARIATE, FALLBACK_BIVARIATE_MIN_ZOOM, FALLBACK_BIVARIATE_MAX_ZOOM, FEATURE_STATES and H3_HOVER_LAYER. A grep shows both prefixes are defined only in src/core/logical_layers/constants.ts:4-5, which is where the removed code imported them from (`'~core/logical_layers/constants'`). getSourcePrefix() and getClickableLayerId() would get undefined, producing source/layer IDs like 'undefined<id>'.

`LAYER_BIVARIATE_PREFIX` and `SOURCE_BIVARIATE_PREFIX` are imported from `./constants` (BivariateRenderer/constants.ts), but that file does not export them. They are defined in `~core/logical_layers/constants`. TypeScript will fail to compile here. Under a transpile-only build, both values are `undefined`, so the source and layer IDs become `undefined<id>`. This contradicts the claim that `pnpm lint:js` and `pnpm coverage` passed. `LAYER_BIVARIATE_PREFIX` and `SOURCE_BIVARIATE_PREFIX` are imported from `./constants` (BivariateRenderer/constants.ts), but that file does not export them. Import the bivariate prefixes from their defining module `./constants` exports neither `LAYER_BIVARIATE_PREFIX` nor `SOURCE_BIVARIATE_PREFIX`; both are defined in `~core/logical_layers/constants`, which the previous implementation imported. This breaks TypeScript checking and module loading for the renderer. Restore the import from the defining module.

legendToMultivariateStyle sets the class thresholds to the axis steps, which are in raw units, but builds the score and base expressions from max-min-normalised MCDA layers. Hexagons are compared against the wrong scale, so bivariate layers are coloured into the wrong legend cells. Lines 9-10 build layers with createMCDALayersFromBivariateAxes, which sets `normalization: 'max-min'` (createMCDALayersFromBivariateAxes.ts:34). linearNormalization then gives roughly 0..1 values (utils/multivariate/multivariateStyle.ts:103-104). Lines 37-40 still pass `scoreSteps: legend.axis.x.steps, baseSteps: legend.axis.y.steps`. The existing helper createStepsForMCDADimension uses axis steps only when `normalization === 'no'` and otherwise uses the default 0..1 steps. The removed code coloured from raw quotient values with generateLayerFromLegend. Example: the test uses axis steps [0, 10], so every normalised value ≤1 falls into the first class.

This conversion changes how every bivariate layer is coloured. The old renderer classified the raw ratio numerator/denominator against `legend.axis.{x,y}.steps`, which are in raw data units. The new style builds MCDA score and base dimensions (`createMCDALayersFromBivariateAxes`), and `createBivariateMultivariateStyle` turns them into normalized max-min values (roughly 0..1, using the sigma range or transformation). Those normalized values are then classified against `stepOverrides` set to the raw axis steps. The units don't match: for example, population density steps of 0/10/100… compared with values in 0..1 put nearly every hexagon in the first class. The fill filter also changes from `filterSetup` to `mcdaFilterSetup`. The unit test only checks the object's shape, so it can't catch this. Keep axis calculations in the same units as legend thresholds `createMCDALayersFromBivariateAxes` enables max-min normalization, clamping, and potentially sentiment inversion, but these overrides retain the original axis thresholds. The multivariate style compares normalized scores against those raw thresholds, so an axis with thresholds such as 10 and 100 will classify every score in the lowest bucket instead of preserving the original bivariate colors. Popup cell classification has the same mismatch. Preserve the original axis-value semantics or convert the thresholds consistently with the score calculation.

The tile source maxzoom for bivariate and MCDA layers now falls back to 9 instead of the indicators' maxZoom. Layers whose data goes beyond zoom 9 get over-zoomed tiles. ClickableFeaturesRenderer.createTileSource uses `layer.maxZoom || this.getMaxZoomLevel(layer)`. MultivariateRenderer.getMaxZoomLevel returns FALLBACK_BIVARIATE_MAX_ZOOM (9) unless `layer.style?.type === 'multivariate'`. Here `layer` is the unconverted `state.source`: the wrapper converts only `state.style`, not `state.source.style`. The removed code used `getMaxNumeratorZoomLevel([legend.axis.x.quotients, legend.axis.y.quotients], …)` for bivariate and `getMaxMCDAZoomLevel(style.config, …)` for MCDA.

The tile source max zoom regresses. The old code used `getMaxNumeratorZoomLevel(legend quotients)` for bivariate layers and `getMaxMCDAZoomLevel(style.config)` for MCDA layers. The new code inherits `MultivariateRenderer.getMaxZoomLevel`, which reads `layer.style` from the tile source, not the converted state style. For bivariate and MCDA layers that check is not `'multivariate'`, so it always falls back to `FALLBACK_BIVARIATE_MAX_ZOOM` (9). Layers whose indicators exist only at lower zooms will request tiles that don't exist, or will stop overzooming correctly. The tile source max zoom regresses. Pass the converted style through to source zoom calculation When a source has no explicit `maxZoom`, the inherited `MultivariateRenderer.getMaxZoomLevel` inspects `state.source.style`, not `state.style`. Only the latter is converted here, so legacy bivariate or MCDA sources take the fallback maximum zoom of 9 instead of the indicator-derived maximum used previously. This can request unsupported tiles or prematurely overzoom lower-resolution tiles. Ensure source creation receives the converted style or retain the legacy zoom calculation.

On a source update, bivariate layers now lose their hover and active feature-state listeners. The inherited addPopup clears every listener, and addHoverAndActiveFeatureState returns early because the border layer already exists, so the listeners are never re-registered. ClickableFeaturesRenderer._updateMap calls `this.addPopup(map, style)`, which runs `this.cleanUpListeners()` and so removes the click/mousemove/mouseleave handlers that addHoverAndActiveFeatureState registered. It then calls addHoverAndActiveFeatureState, which does `if (map.getLayer(borderLayerId)) return;` before registering listeners. The removed addBivariatePopup deleted only its own previous click handler (`this._listenersCleaningTasks.delete(this.removeBivariatePopupClickHandler)`), so hover state survived willSourceUpdate.

The rewrite changes user-visible popups for every layer that uses BivariateRenderer. Bivariate hexes no longer show MapHexTooltip with the computed x/y quotient values, and MCDA layers (mcdaLayer.ts:83) no longer show the MCDA popup. Both now get the generic multivariate popup and fire the 'mcda_popup' metric. No test or acceptance evidence covers these changes. The removed addBivariatePopup rendered `<MapHexTooltip cellLabel… values={{ x: xValue, y: yValue }} hexagonColor={rgba}/>`, and the removed addMCDAPopup used `generateMCDAPopupContent(feature, style.config.layers)`. Now ClickableFeaturesRenderer.addPopup → MultivariateRenderer.createPopupContent → generateMultivariatePopupContent, followed by `dispatchMetricsEvent('mcda_popup')` for every popup, including bivariate ones.

This is a user-visible behaviour change presented as a refactor. The bivariate popup (`MapHexTooltip`) showed the x/y ratio values, the legend cell and the hex colour; it is replaced by the generic multivariate/MCDA popup that shows normalized scores. MCDA layers created in `features/mcda/atoms/mcdaLayer.ts` now get the multivariate popup instead of `generateMCDAPopupContent`. The PR summary doesn't mention either change. A bivariate layer with no legend now silently renders nothing. Previously it failed loudly. convertStyle returns null when neither an mcda style nor a legend is present, and ClickableFeaturesRenderer._updateMap skips mountLayers/addPopup when `style` is falsy. The removed mountBivariateLayer threw `new Error('[Bivariate …] Vector layers must have legend')`.

The new MCDARenderer class and its index are dead code: nothing instantiates them, and MCDA layers still go through BivariateRenderer. A grep for `new MCDARenderer` finds no matches. mcdaLayer.ts:83 still registers `renderer: new BivariateRenderer({ id })`. MCDARenderer also duplicates BivariateRenderer's willSourceUpdate/willMount conversion wrappers.

`MCDARenderer` is new but nothing uses it: `mcdaLayer.ts` and `getLayerRenderer.ts` still create `BivariateRenderer`. It also hardcodes ad-hoc ID prefixes (`'mcda-source-'`, `'mcda-layer-'`) rather than shared constants. Either wire it up or drop it from this PR. `MCDARenderer` is new but nothing uses it: `mcdaLayer.ts` and `getLayerRenderer.ts` still create `BivariateRenderer`. It also hardcodes ad-hoc ID prefixes (`'mcda-source-'`, `'mcda-layer-'`) rather than shared constants. Either wire it up or drop it from this PR.

The new tests check only the object shape returned by the converters. They mock createDefaultMCDAConfig and never check the generated layers' normalisation against the steps, or any renderer behaviour, so they would pass with the scale mismatch and the broken import above. The test uses `toMatchObject` on id/name/colors/stepOverrides, and `score`/`base` are asserted only as `{ type: 'mcda' }`. There are no tests for BivariateRenderer, MCDARenderer, popup content, zoom levels or listener handling, although the old 485-line renderer was replaced.

The test mocks `createDefaultMCDAConfig` and `nanoid`, and only uses `toMatchObject` on the shape of the output. It never checks that the converted style renders like the old bivariate style (for example, by comparing the classification expression or step units). As a result it can't catch the rendering regression above. The test mocks `createDefaultMCDAConfig` and `nanoid`, and only uses `toMatchObject` on the shape of the output.
